To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Most (72%) of complex interventions tested prior to their use in a full-scale evaluation trial are tested, but the amount of testing and its quality vary.

(i) most complex intervention trials test the intervention prior to the trial; (ii) testing is often not described adequately; (iii) the amount of testing done varies; and (iv) most authors do not think further testing would have produced better results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the testing of complex interventions before their evaluation in full-scale trials.
the extent to which complex interventions are tested and whether more or better testing would have led a different intervention being tested.
the testing of complex interventions, and the reporting of this testing in published reports.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
complex interventions are tested in a range of ways prior to a full scale trial, and that this testing has a major impact on the design and implementation of the trial.
the amount of testing is not known.
complex interventions are generally tested but that this is not always described in the trial reports.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is not clear whether pre-trial testing of complex interventions is necessary, but it is certainly useful.
we need more trials of complex interventions, and that we need to report them better.
the MRC framework for developing and evaluating complex interventions should be followed, but that the amount of testing should be determined on a trial by trial basis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the UK MRC framework is being used and that it is important for authors to be explicit in their trial report about the extent of the testing that was done.
it is important to describe the testing that has been done, and to describe what was done and why, and to be transparent about the results of the testing, and the impact of those results.
the UK MRC framework for the development of complex interventions has been widely adopted, but the extent to which interventions have been refined and tested varies considerably.
